title: Finora — Auth Sessions
description: The four AuthMetrics counters added alongside the idle-timeout/absolute-session-cap change (24h idle / 30 days absolute, replacing 30 min / 7 days). Answers the question that change was made without: how many users actually hit each limit. This is a measurement dashboard, not an alerting one — there is no established good/bad line for either expiry series yet. See docs/engineering/observability.md §12.

panels.title: Logins (1h)
panels.description: New sessions minted (RefreshTokenService.issue) from any successful sign-in path -- password, Google, Apple, MFA completion, or reactivation. Does not include ordinary token rotation.

panels.title: Refreshes (1h)
panels.description: Refresh tokens rotated successfully -- an existing session staying alive, inside both the idle and absolute windows.

panels.title: Logins vs refreshes
panels.description: A healthy pattern is many refreshes per login -- a session staying alive far more often than it needs to be re-established. A ratio close to 1:1 means sessions rarely survive to be refreshed at all, which is the symptom the idle/absolute timeout change was meant to fix.

panels.title: Idle expiries (24h)
panels.description: Refreshes refused for exceeding the 24-hour idle window (ErrorCode.AUTH_SESSION_IDLE). The number this dashboard exists to watch: if this stays non-trivial, 24h may still be too short for how the app is actually used.

panels.title: Absolute-cap expiries (24h)
panels.description: Refreshes refused for exceeding the 30-day absolute session cap (ErrorCode.AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE) -- expected to track how many users are active for 30+ consecutive days, not a problem signal on its own.

panels.title: Expiries over time
panels.description: Idle vs absolute expiry, split out. A rising idle-expiry rate is the direct signal that the 24-hour window is still too aggressive for real usage patterns; a rising absolute-expiry rate is expected growth as more users cross 30 days of continuous activity.
